subject: Naperville Approves Luxury Apartments Tripling Allowed Units
posts:
Zoning codes are written for public safety and order, until a luxury developer needs a massive variance to maximize profit.

Naperville Approves Luxury Density Variance
Evidence: public zoning, luxury variance, developer profit

Planners claim the massive variance serves modern urban development and brings high-value growth to the city center.
Stated Judgement: (+1.0, +1.0) — Greater Good

The city approves triple the standard density limit for a luxury project, bypassing codes meant to protect public infrastructure.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.5, -1.0) — Greater Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception.
Rules meant to protect the public are discarded to accommodate high-margin private development.
Naperville planners approved a luxury apartment building at CityGate Centre that features more than triple the density typically allowed under city code.

The Bright Side:
Increasing housing density near major transit corridors is generally a positive step for reducing urban sprawl.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
They frame this as a technical planning variance (WHERE). Structurally, it is a preferential rule bypass (HOW).

It is a bait-and-switch: claiming smart growth while delivering exclusive developer extraction.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between public planning standards and private luxury exceptions...
...it plots a direct trajectory toward Greater Evil. Bypassing density codes for luxury projects prioritizes private profit over balanced public infrastructure.

The Unavoidable Truth: Rules are only as strong as the variances you refuse to grant.

The Unavoidable Lie: That this density is for the public good.

Alethekanon:
When regulatory bodies grant extreme variances for luxury projects, they reveal that zoning codes are barriers for the poor but suggestions for the wealthy.

Awwthekanon:
It is sad to see community rules bent for luxury housing while affordable housing needs go unmet. We must build communities that welcome everyone.

Brothekanon:
So the rules say you can build X, but if you're building 'luxury' apartments, you get to build 3X? Sounds like the rules are just for regular people, bro.
